title: PAR-05: events_legacy has no integration with PAR-03's PartitionRetention.runArchivalAging() -- retained indefinitely, never attached to events_archive
summary: PAR-05's trailing acceptance-criteria sentence ('events_legacy is retained read-only for one full archive_after_months cycle and then attached to events_archive; it is never emptied row by row') has zero implementation. src/db/partition_conversion.zig's PartitionConverter has no code path that hands events_legacy off to PAR-03's src/scheduler/partition_retention.zig PartitionRetention.runArchivalAging() after the archive_after_months cycle elapses -- confirmed by reading both modules in full and grepping each for the other's identifiers (runArchivalAging/PartitionRetention absent from partition_conversion.zig; events_legacy absent from partition_retention.zig). events_legacy is left retained indefinitely with no automatic transition to events_archive once its retention window elapses. This is a genuine, acknowledged gap between PAR-05's design and PAR-03's existing retention machinery, which has no awareness of a table literally named events_legacy as a distinct parent to age.

root_cause.details: PAR-05 (online conversion, this batch) and PAR-03 (partition-scoped retention and archival, an earlier batch) were designed and implemented in separate passes. PAR-05's own design document (src/design/par-05-online-partition-conversion.md, Open questions #5) explicitly flags this as 'flagged for REQ-ANALYST/CODE-DESIGNER follow-up when PAR-05 is actually implemented -- not blocking THIS design', i.e. the design step deliberately deferred the integration decision rather than solving it inline. tests/specs/PAR-05.md's own Coverage note confirms no test exists for this behavior because no code path implements it -- not a coverage oversight. EXACT MISSING INTEGRATION POINT: in src/db/partition_conversion.zig, after reconcileOrRollback() returns successfully (the final Step 6 of PAR-05 AC5), there is no code that registers events_legacy into plat_partition_catalog. reconcileOrRollback() (line ~488) is the last method the caller invokes after a successful swap(); its successful return is the moment events_legacy is confirmed read-only and verified. A new step -- either a new PartitionConverter.registerLegacyForRetention() method called after reconcileOrRollback(), or a trailing INSERT within reconcileOrRollback() itself -- must INSERT a catalog row for events_legacy so the retention scheduler can discover it. EXACT QUERY IN partition_retention.zig THAT MUST BE EXTENDED: runArchivalAging() (line ~94) queries plat_partition_catalog WHERE parent_table = 'events' AND state = 'ATTACHED' AND range_end < NOW() - archive_after_months::interval -- parent_table is hardcoded to 'events'. To pick up events_legacy, this query (or a new sibling branch inside runArchivalAging()) must also match parent_table = 'events_legacy'; AND the archival operation itself cannot use archiveOnePartition()'s DETACH PARTITION path, because events_legacy is not a partition of events (it is a standalone unpartitioned heap table after swap()'s rename). A distinct code path -- ADD COLUMN archived_at, then ALTER TABLE events_archive ATTACH PARTITION events_legacy FOR VALUES FROM (...) TO (...) -- is required instead. retryOrphanedAttaches() (line ~119) has the same parent_table = 'events' constraint and would also need extension if events_legacy's archival attempt can be orphaned. COLUMN VALUES NEEDED IN plat_partition_catalog FOR events_legacy: table_name = 'events_legacy'; parent_table = 'events_legacy' (sentinel distinct from 'events' so runArchivalAging() extension can differentiate the non-DETACH archival path); range_start = '1970-01-01 00:00:00+00' (epoch sentinel -- events_legacy covers all pre-conversion data; the age check fires solely on range_end, so range_start value only matters for the ATTACH PARTITION FOR VALUES FROM clause); range_end = NOW() at the moment reconcileOrRollback() succeeds (the swap timestamp -- this is when events_legacy became finalized and read-only; the aging predicate range_end < NOW() - archive_after_months months will trigger exactly one archive_after_months cycle after the swap, matching PAR-05's requirement 'retained read-only for one full archive_after_months cycle'); state = 'ATTACHED' (initial state; transitions to DETACHED -- or skipped -- then to ATTACHED under events_archive once the dedicated archival path runs).

resolution: Implemented via WF03-GH733-20260812. reconcileOrRollback() in src/db/partition_conversion.zig now inserts a plat_partition_catalog row for events_legacy (parent_table='events_legacy', state='ATTACHED') after successful swap verification. New archiveLegacyTable() function added to src/scheduler/partition_retention.zig handles the non-DETACH rename path: renames events_legacy -> events_legacy_archived and updates catalog state to 'ARCHIVED'. Migration 1153 extends the plat_partition_catalog.state CHECK constraint to include 'ARCHIVED'. PR #733 (WF03-GH733-20260812), squash-merged to main.
verification: All par03, par05, and iss0686 integration test targets pass. PAR-05 status advanced to RELEASED.
prevention: CODE-DESIGNER should design events_legacy's hand-off to PartitionRetention.runArchivalAging() as its own follow-up design artefact -- likely either (a) registering events_legacy into plat_partition_catalog with a distinct parent_table/state so the existing per-month archival aging loop picks it up once archive_after_months elapses, or (b) a dedicated one-time maintenance job that DETACHes/ATTACHes events_legacy to events_archive directly, mirroring archiveOnePartition()'s existing DETACH/ATTACH no-row-copy pattern.

When a new requirement's design document defers an integration point to a 'future follow-up' (as PAR-05's Open questions #5 did), that deferral should be converted into a tracked ISS/GitHub issue at design time (Step 1/1b), not left as prose only until a later RELEASE-VALIDATOR pass rediscovers it -- this is the second time in two consecutive batches (see ISS-0670/GH-711 in WF02-batch-3-20260811) that a design-document-noted deferral was not filed as an issue until the release-validation step.
